content: The process of obtaining a homogeneous population of early fourth instar larvae involves several critical steps. First, a large number of egg rafts must be laid and collected on the same day. These egg rafts can be stored at temperatures between 15°C and 18°C to accumulate more eggs for hatching. The first instar larvae, which are fragile, should not be handled. Development to the second instar typically takes 3 to 4 days at a temperature of 25 ± 2°C after the eggs are laid. Once the second instar larvae are ready, they are grouped in trays containing 3 liters of dechlorinated water at a depth of 4 to 6 cm, with 800 to 1,000 larvae per tray. Food, such as yeast extract and dog or cat biscuits, is provided as needed. Early fourth instar larvae, which are suitable for testing, are usually obtained within 7 days, although in some cases, 8 or 9 days may be required. The maximum acceptable levels of microbial contaminants in these preparations have not yet been determined. For fly larvae toxicity testing, it is not necessary to conduct a test if the manufacturer has demonstrated that the Bacillus thuringiensis strain used does not produce beta-exotoxin. Similarly, no test is required for Bacillus sphaericus, as this species is not known to produce exotoxins. To prevent premature degradation of the product, the water content should not exceed 5%. Bioassay remains the most reliable method for measuring the active ingredient in suspension, although simpler methods like gravimetric determination may be used routinely if they yield results equivalent to the bioassay method. In case of disputes, the bioassay method is considered the referee method. Microbial larvicides should be stored at cool temperatures, and accelerated storage stability tests are recommended for rapid checks on product stability. In the absence of standardized methods, it is recommended that the product lose no more than 10% of its biopotency below the labeled value when stored at 5°C for 2 years or at 20–25°C for 1 year. These tests should be performed using representative product samples, and biopotency should be assessed using validated methods. Variations in biopotency test results of up to ±25% must be accounted for when determining potency loss. For bacterial larvicide water-dispersible tablets, the material should consist of a homogeneous mixture of the specified bacterial strain, along with fillers and necessary formulants. The tablets should be dry, unbroken, free-flowing, and free from visible extraneous matter. The active ingredient must comply with identity tests and meet the declared minimum biopotency content, which should not be less than 90% of the labeled value. The material must be free from beta-exotoxin when tested using the fly larvae toxicity test or an equivalent HPLC method. For bioassay testing, the toxicity of Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis (Bti) and Bacillus sphaericus (Bsph) products is determined by comparing mosquito larval mortality caused by the test product with that caused by a reference standard. Reference powders with assigned toxicity values are used for calibration, and the results are expressed as ITU/mg. For Aedes aegypti, eggs are laid on filter paper, dried, and stored for several months. When larvae are needed, the eggs are immersed in dechlorinated water, and larval feed is added 24 hours prior to hatching to synchronize the process. The larvae are then transferred to containers with dechlorinated water and fed sparingly to avoid bacterial overgrowth. Within 5 to 7 days, a homogeneous population of early fourth instars is obtained. For Culex pipiens pipiens larvae, obtaining a homogeneous population of fourth instars is more challenging. A large number of egg rafts must be laid and collected on the same day, and the first instars should not be handled due to their fragility. Development to the second instar takes 3 to 4 days at 25 ± 2°C. The second instars are then grouped in trays with dechlorinated water and fed as needed. Early fourth instars suitable for testing are typically obtained within 7 to 9 days.
